purpose: Risedronate is used to treat and prevent osteoporosis, which is a condition where your bones become weak and brittle. It is also used to treat Paget's disease of the bone, a condition where bones grow abnormally. This medicine helps reduce your risk of breaking a bone, especially in your hip and spine.
how_it_works: Your body is constantly breaking down old bone and building new bone. In osteoporosis, too much bone is being broken down. Risedronate works by slowing down the cells that break your bone apart, called osteoclasts. This helps your body keep more bone, making your bones stronger and less likely to fracture.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects include heartburn, upset stomach, stomach pain, nausea, and diarrhea. Some people may notice back pain, joint pain, or headache. These are usually mild and often improve over time.
warnings: You must take this medicine exactly as directed — swallow it with a full glass of plain water first thing in the morning, and stay upright (sitting or standing) for at least 30 minutes after taking it. Do not take it with food, juice, or other drinks as this stops it from working properly. Rarely, it can cause serious jaw bone problems or unusual thigh bone fractures. Tell your doctor if you have kidney problems, low calcium levels, or trouble swallowing.
typical_dosing: The most common dose for osteoporosis is one 35 mg tablet taken once a week, or one 5 mg tablet taken once every day. There is also a monthly option of 150 mg once a month. Always take it first thing in the morning on an empty stomach with a full glass of plain water, and do not eat or drink anything else for at least 30 minutes afterward.
